title: Artin–Schreier vanishing on a smooth curve
statement:
Let $C$ be a smooth separated connected curve
over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$.
For the constant sheaf
$\mathbf F_p$, one has $H^q(C,\mathbf F_p)=0$ for $q>1$,
with cohomology as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: Obtain the actual Artin-Schreier short exact sequence, with its additive section equivalences and sectionwise Frobenius-minus-identity equation.
Form its single distinguished triangle and apply the triangulated unbounded right derived global-sections functor.
If q=2, the preceding-degree map is epi by the first-cohomology Frobenius lemma. Otherwise q>2, hence q-1>=2, and its target is zero by derived additive vanishing, so it is epi.

The long exact homology sequence makes the connecting map zero when the preceding map is epi. The degree-q additive group is zero. Exactness at H^q(C,Z/p) with both incident maps zero therefore makes that object zero.
